title: The little singing whale
summary: A tiny whale discovers her voice is the most beautiful gift in the ocean.

scenes.text: In the deepest part of the blue sea, where the water is as dark as night but still lets through little sun rays like threads of melted gold, lived a very tiny whale. She was the size of a mattress, with a white belly and a back the color of a stormy sky. High above her, the sea rolled in long, slow waves. But the tiny whale kept a huge secret: she never spoke, she never sang, she never even made bubbles. She was ashamed of her voice because she thought it was too small, too thin, too nothing. Every day she hid behind the pink corals, with her tail curled under her belly, and watched the colorful fish go by without saying hello. "Hello," she wanted to say quietly. But the word got stuck in her throat, like a shy little snail. The ocean watched over her in silence, patient, waiting for the day she would feel brave enough.

One calm morning, while she swam alone among the seaweed, she heard something different. A thin, weeping sound. It was a lost little octopus, sitting on a clam, with all eight of his arms curled up in sadness. His eyes were full of tears that mixed with the salt water. The tiny whale watched him from afar, hesitated for a second, came a little closer, hesitated again. Then she closed her eyes and breathed. And, almost without meaning to, she opened her mouth and sang. Out of her came a trembling, gentle sound, like a sigh of water. The little octopus stopped crying instantly, surprised. He lifted his head, blinked, and waved all his arms at the same time. "Was that you?" he asked quietly, as if he didn't dare believe it. The whale wanted to hide behind the coral again and lowered her head. But the octopus smiled at her with a huge smile, full of tenderness, and said: "It's the most beautiful thing I've ever heard in my life."

The tiny whale stayed very still, not knowing what to say. Her cheeks turned a soft pink, just like the coral next to her. The little octopus sat on a soft stone, crossed two of his arms as if they were legs, and looked at her with the face of a child waiting for a story. "Will you sing again? Please, please," he begged, wiggling his suckers. The whale closed her eyes, filled her lungs with salty water until her heart felt warm, and let out another song. From her mouth rose bubbles. They were blue, pink, gold and silver, and they traveled slowly up to the surface, carrying the music with them. A curious sardine peeked out from behind a coral and stayed to listen, without moving. Then came a green turtle. Then a yellow crab. Then a purple starfish that came down from the sky of the sea. Nobody laughed. Everybody smiled, hypnotized.

The fish kept coming: first ten, then a hundred, then a whole school shining like silver confetti. Dolphins did pirouettes in the water. Seahorses jumped like springs, the seaweed swayed to the rhythm of the melody like green dancers, and even the jellyfish lit up their lights. The tiny whale looked at them all with her eyes wide open, unable to believe it. Her voice, that small voice that had embarrassed her so much, was making the whole ocean happy. The octopus stroked her belly with one arm and said: "See? Your voice wasn't small. It was special." The whale understood, in that moment, that every creature has a gift, and hers was singing. And from that night on, so the ocean could fall asleep in peace, she sang. All the fish in the sea waited for her with their eyes closed, dreaming of her melody.
